newsitem.title: ITALY: Bossi faces trial for insulting Italian president.
newsitem.headline: Bossi faces trial for insulting Italian president.

text.p: A judge on Wednesday ordered separatist Northern League leader Umberto Bossi to stand trial for comparing Italian president Oscar Luigi Scalfaro to Rasputin.
Judge Clementina Forleo ordered the trial, for contempt of the head of state, to start on March 17 next year.

Bossi has already been sentenced to eight months in one court case involving illegal party financing and faces two further cases that have yet to start on charges of incitement to violence, aggravated threats and defamation.

The offending remark, comparing the deeply-religious president to the debauched mystic monk who enthralled the wife of Russia's last Tsar, appeared in an interview with the Milan Corriere della Sera newspaper in 1993.
Earlier this month, Bossi was ordered to stand trial for urging his supporters at a political rally in north-east Italy to "identify and pursue" far-right voters.
That trial is due to start in Tolmezzo on March 27.
Another defamation case against him opens on July 2 in Bergamo.
Bossi, whose League wants independence for Italy's rich north from what he lambasts as a corrupt Rome bureaucracy, has declared a northern state of "Padania".

Public concern about Bossi's behaviour has increased since eight separatist paramilitaries occupied the bell tower in the lagoon city of Venice last month to publicise a drive for an independent Venetian republic.
The eight, who are now on trial, are not directly associated with the League but Bossi's opponents have argued that his secessionist rhetoric has incited hotheads.
